chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who was killed by al-qisas (retaliation/executory death), is there a diya (blood money) for him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it were so, no one would be retaliated against from [the killer], and whoever is killed by the hadd (legal penalty), there is no diya for him.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: A fixed legal penalty prescribed by Sharia for a specific crime
key_terms.الْقِصَاصُ: Retaliation or executory death, specifically for murder
key_terms.دِيَةٌ: Blood money or compensation paid to the heirs

ai.seo_question: Does a person executed for murder receive blood money (diya) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the execution itself serves as the full compensation for the victim, thereby precluding any additional blood money (diya) for those killed via qisas or hadd. This ruling underscores the principle that the punitive measure is the retribution, distinguishing it from cases where diya is paid to heirs for accidental or partial culpability deaths. The hadith highlights the jurisprudential distinction between the penalty being the death itself versus a financial compensation owed for the loss of life.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Zayd Al Shahaam who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man killed by ‘الْقِصَاصُ’ the retaliation, is there a wergild for him?’ Heasws said: ‘If it was like that, no one would be retaliated from, and the one who is killed by the legal penalty (Hadd), so there is no wergild for him’.
